body:
## Problem

fetchArticles dereferences item.PublishedParsed without a nil check. In gofeed, PublishedParsed is a *time.Time that is nil whenever a feed item carries no publication date or one that gofeed cannot parse. pubDate is optional in RSS 2.0 and published is optional in Atom, so a nil value is normal feed data, not a corrupt feed.

## Evidence

main.go:131-141

    for _, item := range feed.Items {
        // Parse publish date
        publishAt := item.PublishedParsed.UTC()

Reproduced against gofeed v1.4.2 (the version pinned in go.mod) with a minimal, valid RSS 2.0 item that omits pubDate:

    <item><title>No date item</title><link>https://example.com/a</link></item>

Output:
    Published="" PublishedParsed==nil? true
    PANIC replicating fetchArticles line 133: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference

## Impact

A single dateless item in any one of the configured feeds panics the process. The panic is not recoverable by the per-feed error handling in main.go:79-82, because that path only handles returned errors, not panics. Every other feed already fetched is discarded, no output file is written, and the previous output.md is left stale. For the cron-driven usage the README recommends, the newsletter silently stops being produced.

## Fix

Skip items with no parseable date, or fall back to UpdatedParsed before skipping:

    for _, item := range feed.Items {
        published := item.PublishedParsed
        if published == nil {
            published = item.UpdatedParsed
        }
        if published == nil {
            log.Printf("skipping %q: no parseable publish date", item.Title)
            continue
        }
        articles = append(articles, Article{
            Title:     item.Title,
            URL:       item.Link,
            PublishAt: published.UTC(),
            URLDomain: getURLDomain(item.Link),
        })
    }

Add a table test over fp.Parse with a dateless item asserting no panic and the item dropped.

## Resolution
itemsToArticles (split out of fetchArticles for testability) now falls back to UpdatedParsed and skips the item with a log line when both are nil. Regression test TestItemsToArticlesSkipsUndatedItems parses a real RSS fixture with no pubDate through gofeed and asserts the item is dropped rather than panicking; TestItemsToArticlesFallsBackToUpdated covers the Atom updated-only shape.
title: Nil dereference on item.PublishedParsed panics the whole run

body:
## Problem

getURLDomain ignores the error from url.Parse and immediately reads read.Host. url.Parse returns a nil *url.URL together with its error, so any link that fails to parse produces a nil pointer dereference rather than a degraded domain string. Feed item links are remote, untrusted input.

## Evidence

main.go:196-208

    if regexp.MustCompile(`^https?`).MatchString(urlString) {
        read, _ := url.Parse(urlString)
        urlString = read.Host
    }

Reproduced with the function copied verbatim and given a link with a malformed percent-escape, which is accepted by feed parsers but rejected by url.Parse:

    parse err=parse "https://example.com/%zz": invalid URL escape "%zz"  u==nil? true
    PANIC in getURLDomain: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference

## Impact

Same blast radius as the PublishedParsed panic: one malformed link anywhere in any configured feed kills the process, discards every feed already fetched, and leaves the output file stale. Because getURLDomain is called from fetchArticles (main.go:134), the per-feed continue in main cannot contain it.

## Fix

Handle the error and fall through to the raw string, which the trailing domain regexp already tolerates:

    if strings.HasPrefix(urlString, "http://") || strings.HasPrefix(urlString, "https://") {
        if read, err := url.Parse(urlString); err == nil {
            urlString = read.Host
        }
    }

Note the prefix check also fixes a second defect in the same branch: the regexp `^https?` matches any string starting with "http", so "httpfoo" enters the parse branch and yields an empty Host. Add unit tests for a malformed URL, a bare domain, a www-prefixed host, and the empty string.

## Resolution
getURLDomain now checks the url.Parse error and falls through to the raw string on failure. The `^https?` regexp was also replaced with strings.HasPrefix checks for "http://" and "https://", fixing the secondary defect where "httpfoo" entered the parse branch. Covered by TestGetURLDomain cases "malformed percent escape" and "http-prefixed non-URL".
title: getURLDomain discards the url.Parse error and dereferences a nil *url.URL

body:
## Problem

generateMarkdown writes item.Title and item.Link straight into a Markdown link construct with fmt.Sprintf and no escaping or newline stripping. Feed content is fully controlled by whoever operates the feed, so the trust boundary between remote feed data and the generated document is unguarded.

## Evidence

main.go:182

    output.WriteString(fmt.Sprintf("- %s @ %s: [%s](%s)\n", article.PublishAt.Format("2006-01-02"), article.URLDomain, article.Title, article.URL))

Reproduced with a title containing newlines and Markdown syntax:

    title := "Benign title\n\n## Week: 2099-99\n\n- [Click me](https://evil.example/phish)"

Rendered fragment:

    - 2026-08-28 @ feed.example: [Benign title

    ## Week: 2099-99

    - [Click me](https://evil.example/phish)](https://feed.example/post)

The injected heading and link are now structural elements of the document, not link text.

## Impact

A compromised or hostile feed controls the structure of output.md: it can forge week headings, insert arbitrary links pointing anywhere, and break the enclosing link so the real source URL is displayed as literal text. The README recommends mailing this output on a cron schedule, so the rendered result reaches a reader's inbox as HTML, where an injected link is an ordinary phishing vector. Even without an adversary, any title containing "]" or a link containing ")" or a space corrupts the entry, which is common in real feeds.

## Fix

Sanitize both fields at the render boundary. Collapse whitespace and escape the Markdown link delimiters in the title; percent-encode or reject a link that is not a clean absolute URL:

    func mdText(s string) string {
        s = strings.Join(strings.Fields(s), " ") // collapses newlines and runs of space
        r := strings.NewReplacer("[", "\\[", "]", "\\]")
        return r.Replace(s)
    }

    func mdURL(raw string) string {
        u, err := url.Parse(strings.TrimSpace(raw))
        if err != nil || (u.Scheme != "http" && u.Scheme != "https") {
            return ""
        }
        return u.String() // already escapes spaces and parentheses in the path
    }

Emit the entry as plain text when mdURL returns empty. Cover both helpers with tests for a newline-bearing title, a bracket-bearing title, and a javascript: link.

## Resolution
Added mdText (collapses whitespace runs including newlines, escapes [ and ]) and mdURL (rejects any scheme but http/https, percent-encodes space, parens and angle brackets). generateMarkdown routes both remote fields through them and renders the entry as plain text when the link is rejected. Note the escaped title text still contains the injected characters verbatim — that is correct, escaping neutralizes structure rather than censoring the title; the test asserts structure (exactly one heading line, one list-item line, and the item ending in the legitimate link target) rather than substring absence.
title: Untrusted feed titles and links are interpolated into Markdown unescaped

body:
## Problem

There are zero _test.go files in the repository, and .github/workflows/test-build.yml never invokes go test despite being named "Test Build and Run". The three functions with non-trivial logic — fetchArticles, generateMarkdown, getURLDomain — are entirely unexercised by automated checks.

## Evidence

find . -name '*_test.go' | wc -l  ->  0

.github/workflows/test-build.yml steps are: checkout, setup-go, "make build", "cp examples/* .", "./paperboy". No go test, go vet, or lint step exists.

Both Critical findings in this audit (audit-b972f3ed, audit-2de2c1ba) are single-line nil dereferences that a three-line unit test would have caught at introduction.

## Impact

No regression protection on the only logic in the project. The current CI step substitutes for tests by fetching six live third-party feeds over the network on every push and pull request, which makes CI both non-hermetic and non-deterministic: it fails when an unrelated third party is down, and it passes when every feed fails, because fetchArticles errors are logged and skipped at main.go:79-82 and an output file is still written. The pipeline therefore cannot distinguish a working build from a completely broken one.

## Fix

Add main_test.go covering, at minimum: getURLDomain over a table (https URL, www-prefixed, bare domain, malformed percent-escape, empty string); generateMarkdown against a temp template file for the valid case, a template with fewer than two "---" separators, and an empty week map; and fetchArticles logic against gofeed's fp.Parse with a fixture feed that omits pubDate. Extract the item loop out of fetchArticles so it can be tested without network I/O. Add to the workflow before the build step:

      - name: Test
        run: go test ./...

      - name: Vet
        run: go vet ./...

Keep the live-feed smoke run if desired, but it must not be the only signal.

## Resolution
Added main_test.go: 42 subtests over getURLDomain, itemsToArticles (via gofeed fixtures, no network), mdText, mdURL, loadTemplate, loadConfig and generateMarkdown. Added "go vet" and "go test ./..." steps to the CI workflow ahead of the build, plus test and lint targets to the Makefile. The live-feed run is kept as a smoke test with a comment stating it is not a correctness signal. go test, go vet, gofmt -l and golangci-lint are all clean.
title: Repository has no tests; CI workflow named "Test" runs none

body:
## Problem

fetchArticles uses gofeed.NewParser() with every field left at its zero value. Parser.MaxByteSize defaults to 0, which the library documents as "no limit", so the whole response body of an untrusted remote server is read into memory before parsing.

## Evidence

main.go:123-128

    fp := gofeed.NewParser()
    feed, err := fp.ParseURL(feedURL)

gofeed v1.4.2 parser.go:53-57:

    // MaxByteSize limits how many bytes ParseURL/ParseURLWithContext will read
    // from a response body. Zero means no limit. Exceeding it returns
    // ErrResponseTooLarge rather than silently truncating.
    MaxByteSize int64

Note the request timeout is NOT a gap here: gofeed v1.4.2 applies a 30s defaultRequestTimeout inside ParseURL (parser.go:23, 135-138), so a slow server is already bounded. Only the response size is unbounded.

## Impact

A feed server that is compromised, misconfigured, or simply serving a large error page streams unbounded bytes into the process. On a small cron host this is an OOM kill, which has the same outcome as the two panic findings: no output written and a stale output.md. The 30s timeout does not bound this, because a fast server can deliver a great deal of data well within 30s.

## Fix

Set an explicit ceiling and a User-Agent on the parser, and hoist it out of the per-feed call so it is constructed once:

    fp := gofeed.NewParser()
    fp.MaxByteSize = 16 << 20 // 16 MiB; largest observed real feed is far below this
    fp.UserAgent = fmt.Sprintf("paperboy/%s (+https://github.com/ivuorinen/paperboy)", version)

ErrResponseTooLarge then surfaces through the existing error return at main.go:79-82 and the feed is skipped rather than taking down the run.

## Resolution
The parser is now built once in main with MaxByteSize set to 16 MiB (maxFeedBytes) and an explicit UserAgent, then passed into fetchArticles. gofeed returns ErrResponseTooLarge, which surfaces through the existing per-feed error path and skips the feed instead of taking down the run.
title: Feed parser reads remote responses with no size limit
generateMarkdown calls log.Fatalf, discarding every feed already fetched

body:
## Problem

The comment states both variables are set during build time. Only version is. The build variable is initialized by time.Now() during package initialization, so it records the moment the binary was started, not when it was compiled, and the Makefile's ldflags never references it.

## Evidence

main.go:29-34

    // Version and Build information
    // These variables are set during build time
    var (
        version string = "dev"
        build   string = time.Now().Format("20060102")
    )

Makefile:9-12 sets only version:

    go build -o paperboy \
      -ldflags "-X main.version=${VERSION}" \
        main.go

Note that -X could not set build even if it were listed, because -X only overwrites a string variable whose initializer is a constant; time.Now() is not, so the linker would silently ignore it.

## Impact

The banner logged at main.go:52 reports today's date as the build date for every run, so a binary compiled months ago claims to have been built this morning. Anyone diagnosing a report against a deployed binary gets a value that is not merely stale but actively misleading, and the comment tells them to trust it. The CI workflow also never passes VERSION, so released binaries additionally report version "dev".

## Fix

Make build genuinely link-time settable and stamp both in the Makefile:

    // version and build are stamped by the linker; see the build target in the
    // Makefile. Both must stay constant-initialized or -X is silently ignored.
    var (
        version = "dev"
        build   = "unknown"
    )

    build: # Build the binary. Use VERSION (make build VERSION=1.2.3) to set the build version.
        go build -o paperboy \
          -ldflags "-X main.version=$(VERSION) -X main.build=$(shell date -u +%Y%m%d)" \
          .

This also drops the redundant explicit "string" type on both declarations.

## Resolution
build is now constant-initialized to "unknown" so -X can set it, and the Makefile stamps both: -X main.version=$(VERSION) -X main.build=$(BUILD) with BUILD defaulting to $(shell date -u +%Y%m%d). The misleading comment is replaced with one stating why constant initialization is required. Verified: "make build VERSION=1.2.3" produces a binary logging "Paperboy v.1.2.3 (build 20260828)". Redundant explicit string types dropped.
title: Comment claims build and version are set at build time; build is a runtime timestamp

body:
## Problem

The README instructs the user to create template.md and config.yaml "in the same directory as the binary". The program resolves neither path relative to the executable: it reads the bare relative name "config.yaml", which the OS resolves against the process working directory, and the template path from config is likewise relative to the working directory.

## Evidence

.github/README.md:7

    Create `template.md` and `config.yaml` in the same directory as the binary.

main.go:55-56

    configFile := "config.yaml"
    configData, err := os.ReadFile(configFile)

main.go:150 resolves the template the same way, and main.go:112-113 writes config.Output the same way. Nothing in main.go consults os.Executable.

## Impact

The documented layout fails in exactly the deployment the README recommends two paragraphs later: "Use a cron job to run this weekly". A crontab entry runs with the working directory set to the user's home, so a binary installed in /usr/local/bin with its config beside it exits immediately at main.go:58 with "Error reading config.yaml file". The operator follows the documentation correctly and the tool does not work.

## Fix

Correct the sentence and state the real requirement, in the README:

    Create `template.md` and `config.yaml` in the directory you run `paperboy`
    from. Paths in `config.yaml` are resolved relative to that working
    directory, not to the binary's location. For a cron entry, `cd` first:

        0 8 * * 1 cd /srv/paperboy && /usr/local/bin/paperboy

Better, remove the constraint rather than document it: accept an optional config path argument, which is a four-line change at main.go:55 using flag.StringVar with "config.yaml" as the default. That also resolves the related gap that the config path is otherwise unoverridable.

## Resolution
README now states paths resolve against the working directory, not the binary's location, and the cron ProTip carries a worked crontab line that cds first. Also took the finding's preferred option: added a -config flag defaulting to config.yaml, so the constraint can be sidestepped entirely. Verified both the flag and the error path against the built binary.
title: README says config lives beside the binary; the code reads it from the working directory

body:
## Problem

test-build.yml sets no permissions key at either workflow or job level, so GITHUB_TOKEN is granted whatever the repository or organization default is. Where that default is still "read and write", the token handed to this job can push commits, alter releases, and edit issues, none of which a build-and-run job needs.

## Evidence

.github/workflows/test-build.yml:1-13 — the file goes straight from the "on:" trigger block to "jobs:", with no permissions key anywhere:

    on:
      push:
        branches: ["main"]
      pull_request:
        branches: ["main"]

    jobs:
      test-build-and-run:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest

The job's only needs are checking out the repository and reading the module cache.

## Impact

The workflow runs on pull_request, so it executes with a token scoped to this repository on every contributor PR. Any compromised step — a tampered action, or a malicious module pulled during "make build", which runs before any pinning check — can use that token at full default scope. Declaring least privilege removes the escalation regardless of what the repository default happens to be set to today, and stops a later change to that default from silently widening this job.

## Fix

Add a top-level permissions block immediately after the "on:" section:

    permissions:
      contents: read

Nothing in the job writes to the repository, so no job-level override is needed. The two actions in use are already pinned to full commit SHAs (checkout@3d3c42e, setup-go@b7ad1dad), which is correct and should be kept.

## Resolution
Added a top-level "permissions: contents: read" block to test-build.yml. No job needs write access; the two actions remain pinned to full commit SHAs.
title: Workflow declares no permissions block, inheriting the repository default token scope

body:
## Problem

The workflow installs Go 1.26, but go.mod declares "toolchain go1.27.0". Under the default GOTOOLCHAIN=auto, the 1.26 toolchain that setup-go installed does not build the module; it downloads go1.27.0 at build time and re-execs into it. The version the workflow pins is therefore not the version that compiles the code.

## Evidence

.github/workflows/test-build.yml:16-19

      - name: Set up Go
        uses: actions/setup-go@b7ad1dad31e06c5925ef5d2fc7ad053ef454303e # v7
        with:
          go-version: "1.26"

go.mod:3-5

    go 1.25.0

    toolchain go1.27.0

The most recent commit, 8dc09ea, is titled "chore(go): set language floor to 1.25.0 and track toolchain go1.27.0" — the workflow was not updated alongside it.

## Impact

The pin is decorative: it neither controls the compiler actually used nor fails when it disagrees with go.mod, so the drift is invisible. Every CI run pays an unnecessary toolchain download, and setup-go's module cache is keyed on a Go version that is not the one building, weakening cache reuse. If GOTOOLCHAIN is ever set to local — the standard hardening for hermetic or air-gapped builds — the job stops failing silently and starts failing outright with a toolchain error.

## Fix

Point setup-go at go.mod so the two can never drift again:

      - name: Set up Go
        uses: actions/setup-go@b7ad1dad31e06c5925ef5d2fc7ad053ef454303e # v7
        with:
          go-version-file: go.mod

setup-go honours the toolchain line, so this installs go1.27.0 directly and removes the redundant download. It also means the Renovate updates that bump go.mod need no matching workflow edit.

## Resolution
Replaced the hardcoded go-version: "1.26" with go-version-file: go.mod, so setup-go reads the go and toolchain lines directly and the two can no longer drift. Renovate bumps to go.mod now need no matching workflow edit.
title: CI pins Go 1.26 while go.mod requires toolchain go1.27.0

body:
## Problem

After yaml.Unmarshal succeeds, no field of Config is checked. A config file that parses but omits output, template, or feeds — or misspells any of those keys — leaves the corresponding field at its zero value and the program proceeds as if it were configured.

## Evidence

main.go:62-66 accepts whatever unmarshals:

    var config Config
    err = yaml.Unmarshal(configData, &config)
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatalf("Error parsing config.yaml file: %v", err)
    }

The zero values then reach three different consumers unchecked: config.Feeds at main.go:74, config.Template at main.go:107 (via generateMarkdown), and config.Output at main.go:112-113:

    outputFile := config.Output
    err = os.WriteFile(outputFile, []byte(output), 0644)

yaml.v3 ignores unknown keys by default, so "outout: news.md" unmarshals cleanly and leaves Output empty.

## Impact

Each missing field fails late and obscurely rather than at startup. A misspelled output key fetches every feed, renders the document, then dies at main.go:115 with "Error writing output file: open : no such file or directory" — an error naming an empty path, after all the network work is done. An empty feeds list produces a valid document containing only the header and footer, with no warning that nothing was configured, which under cron silently overwrites a good output.md with an empty one.

## Fix

Validate immediately after unmarshalling, before any feed is fetched:

    switch {
    case len(config.Feeds) == 0:
        log.Fatalf("%s: no feeds configured", configFile)
    case config.Template == "":
        log.Fatalf("%s: template is required", configFile)
    case config.Output == "":
        log.Fatalf("%s: output is required", configFile)
    }

Also set KnownFields so a misspelled key is an error rather than a silent omission, which is the defect that makes this class of mistake hard to spot:

    dec := yaml.NewDecoder(bytes.NewReader(configData))
    dec.KnownFields(true)
    if err := dec.Decode(&config); err != nil { ... }

## Resolution
Config handling moved into loadConfig, which decodes with KnownFields(true) and then requires feeds, template and output, naming the file and the missing key. io.EOF from an empty file is allowed through so the required-field check reports "no feeds configured" rather than "EOF". Covered by TestLoadConfig, including the misspelled-key case. Verified against the binary: the "outout" typo now fails immediately with "field outout not found in type main.Config".
title: Config is unmarshalled without validating any required field

body:
## Problem

The two sort directions in the output disagree. Weeks are sorted ascending then reversed, giving newest week first. Articles inside each week are sorted by ascending timestamp, giving oldest article first. The reader scrolls backwards through time between sections and forwards through time within them.

## Evidence

main.go:100-102 — weeks, descending:

    sort.Strings(weeks)
    slices.Reverse(weeks)

main.go:175-178 — articles, ascending:

    slices.SortFunc(articles, func(a, b Article) int {
        return cmp.Compare(a.PublishAt.Unix(), b.PublishAt.Unix())
    })

No comment marks either direction as deliberate.

## Impact

In the newest week — the section a weekly newsletter reader actually reads — the most recent article is at the bottom of the list rather than the top. The inconsistency is silent: there is no test asserting either order, so whichever direction was intended, nothing records or protects it.

## Fix

Make both descending, and compare the times directly rather than through Unix seconds, which discards sub-second precision and ties items published in the same second arbitrarily:

    slices.SortFunc(articles, func(a, b Article) int {
        return b.PublishAt.Compare(a.PublishAt)
    })

If oldest-first within a week is the intent, keep a.PublishAt.Compare(b.PublishAt) and add a comment saying so. Either way assert the chosen order in a generateMarkdown test.

## Resolution
Articles are now sorted newest-first with b.PublishAt.Compare(a.PublishAt), matching the descending week order, and comparing time.Time directly rather than through Unix seconds so sub-second precision is no longer discarded. The chosen order is asserted by TestGenerateMarkdown/orders_weeks_and_articles_newest_first, which checks the positions of both week headings and both article titles.
title: Weeks are ordered newest-first but articles within a week oldest-first

body:
## Problem

The [*] section sets indent_style = space with no [*.go] override. Go's canonical formatting, produced by gofmt and enforced by every Go toolchain and linter, indents with tabs. The repository's only source file is therefore configured against the format the language requires.

## Evidence

.editorconfig:3-11

    [*]
    charset = utf-8
    end_of_line = lf
    indent_size = 2
    indent_style = space
    ...

    [Makefile]
    tab_width = 4

A [Makefile] override exists — so the tab-sensitive case was noticed — but no [*.go] section does. main.go is currently tab-indented and gofmt-clean (gofmt -l reports nothing), meaning the checked-in file already violates the declared config.

## Impact

Any editor honouring .editorconfig reindents main.go with spaces on save, gofmt converts it back, and the file churns between the two on every edit. The Makefile override is also incomplete: it sets tab_width but leaves indent_style = space inherited, so a Make recipe saved by such an editor gets space-indented and Make rejects it with "missing separator".

## Fix

Add a Go section and complete the Makefile one:

    [*.go]
    indent_style = tab
    indent_size = 4

    [Makefile]
    indent_style = tab
    tab_width = 4

## Resolution
Added an [*.go] section with indent_style = tab, and completed the [Makefile] section with the indent_style = tab it was inheriting as space. gofmt -l stays clean.
title: .editorconfig mandates space indentation for all files, contradicting gofmt
getURLDomain recompiles four regexps on every article

body:
## Problem

main tracks week identifiers twice: once as the keys of articlesByWeek and again in a parallel weeks slice, kept unique by a slices.Contains scan on every article. The slice carries no information the map does not already hold.

## Evidence

main.go:71-102

    articlesByWeek := make(map[string][]Article)
    var weeks []string
    ...
            articlesByWeek[id] = append(articlesByWeek[id], article)

            if !slices.Contains(weeks, id) {
                weeks = append(weeks, id)
            }
    ...
    sort.Strings(weeks)
    slices.Reverse(weeks)

The dead-branch guard at main.go:171-173 confirms the redundancy — it skips empty weeks, a state the map cannot produce, since a key only exists once an article has been appended to it.

## Impact

Two structures that must be kept in agreement by hand, where one derived value would do. The Contains scan makes grouping O(articles x weeks) instead of O(articles); irrelevant at current scale, but it is extra code buying nothing. This also mixes the deprecated sort.Strings with the slices package used everywhere else in the same function.

## Fix

Derive the ordering from the map at the point of use and delete the slice, the Contains check, and the empty guard:

    import "maps"

    weeks := slices.Sorted(maps.Keys(articlesByWeek))
    slices.Reverse(weeks)

Both maps.Keys and slices.Sorted are available under the declared go 1.25.0 floor. If generateMarkdown is changed to take only the map, it can do this itself and main need not compute weeks at all.

## Resolution
The weeks slice, the slices.Contains scan and the dead empty-week guard in generateMarkdown are all deleted. Ordering is now derived from the map at the point of use: slices.Sorted(maps.Keys(articlesByWeek)) followed by slices.Reverse. This also removes the last sort.Strings call, so the file no longer mixes the sort and slices packages.
title: The weeks slice duplicates the map keys and is maintained with a linear scan per article

body:
## Problem

Three idiom violations that the repository's own installed linter reports or that break the standard errors API. fetchArticles formats the underlying error with %v, which flattens it to a string and severs the error chain. Two WriteString(fmt.Sprintf(...)) calls allocate an intermediate string for no reason.

## Evidence

golangci-lint 2.13.1, run against the repository:

    main.go:180:3: QF1012: Use fmt.Fprintf(...) instead of WriteString(fmt.Sprintf(...)) (staticcheck)
    main.go:182:4: QF1012: Use fmt.Fprintf(...) instead of WriteString(fmt.Sprintf(...)) (staticcheck)
    2 issues

main.go:126-128, not reported by the default linter set but wrong regardless:

    if err != nil {
        return nil, fmt.Errorf("error fetching feed: %v", err)
    }

go vet and gofmt -l are both clean.

## Impact

The %v wrap means errors.Is and errors.As cannot see through to the cause, so a caller cannot distinguish gofeed's ErrResponseTooLarge or a context deadline from an HTTP 404 without string matching. That blocks the per-error-class handling the fix for audit-34615984 assumes. The two QF1012 hits mean a lint step added to CI starts red, which is a reason not to add one.

## Fix

main.go:127 — use %w and drop the redundant "error" prefix, since the caller at main.go:80 already prints "Error fetching articles from %s":

    return nil, fmt.Errorf("parsing feed: %w", err)

main.go:180 and 182 — write directly into the builder:

    fmt.Fprintf(&output, "## Week: %s\n\n", week)
    fmt.Fprintf(&output, "- %s @ %s: [%s](%s)\n", article.PublishAt.Format("2006-01-02"), article.URLDomain, article.Title, article.URL)

Then add "golangci-lint run" to the CI workflow so the clean state is held.

## Resolution
fetchArticles now wraps with %w and drops the duplicated "error" prefix, so errors.Is can reach gofeed.ErrResponseTooLarge and context deadlines. Both WriteString(fmt.Sprintf(...)) calls became fmt.Fprintf(&output, ...). golangci-lint 2.13.1 reports "0 issues"; go vet and gofmt -l are clean. A lint target was added to the Makefile and a vet step to CI to hold this.
title: Error wrapped with %v instead of %w, and two staticcheck QF1012 violations

body:
## Problem

Two defects in the same four lines. The build target is absent from .PHONY, which lists only help. And it names main.go explicitly rather than building the package, so the build's file set is a hand-maintained list of one.

## Evidence

Makefile:5-12

    .PHONY: help
    help: # Show help for each of the Makefile recipes.
        ...

    build: # Build the binary. Use VERSION (make build VERSION=1.2.3) to set the build version.
        go build -o paperboy \
          -ldflags "-X main.version=${VERSION}" \
            main.go

.gitignore:5 ignores the "paperboy" output, so the artifact is untracked but still lands in the working tree beside the Makefile.

## Impact

The moment a second .go file is added to package main — which the tests filed as audit-1bd4a028 will require, and any refactor extracting helpers will too — "make build" fails with undefined-symbol errors, while "go build ./..." succeeds. That failure looks like a code error rather than a Makefile omission. Separately, because build is not .PHONY and the target name matches nothing on disk today, the target silently becomes a no-op if a file or directory named "build" is ever created.

## Fix

Declare the target phony and build the package:

    .PHONY: help build

    build: # Build the binary. Use VERSION (make build VERSION=1.2.3) to set the build version.
        go build -o paperboy \
          -ldflags "-X main.version=$(VERSION)" \
          .

Note "." rather than "main.go". While editing, prefer $(VERSION) over ${VERSION}: both work in GNU Make, but the parenthesized form is the convention and avoids being read as a shell variable.

## Resolution
.PHONY now lists help, build, test and lint. The build target compiles the package (".") instead of main.go, which the new main_test.go made necessary immediately. ${VERSION} changed to $(VERSION). Verified "make build VERSION=1.2.3" produces a working binary.
title: build target is not .PHONY and compiles a file list instead of the package

body:
## Problem

main.go carries a //go:build go1.22 constraint while go.mod declares go 1.25.0. The constraint can never exclude a toolchain the module already permits, so it gates nothing.

## Evidence

main.go:9

    //go:build go1.22

go.mod:3

    go 1.25.0

The build tag is also the only one in the repository, on the only file in the package — so if a toolchain ever did fail it, the package would have no files at all and fail with "build constraints exclude all Go files" rather than a version message.

## Impact

No runtime effect today; this is dead metadata that misstates the project's requirements to a reader. Its risk is directional: it says 1.22 while the code already uses cmp and slices under a 1.25 floor, so anyone trusting the tag over go.mod draws the wrong conclusion about what this file needs.

## Fix

Delete line 9 and the blank line following it. go.mod is the single authority for the language floor, and Renovate is already keeping it current (commits db98028 and 8dc09ea). Keep a per-file build constraint only when a file genuinely must be excluded on some toolchain, which is not the case here.

## Resolution
Removed the //go:build go1.22 line and its trailing blank line. go.mod is now the single authority for the language floor. Build and tests pass without it.
title: Stale //go:build go1.22 constraint sits below the module's declared floor

body:
## Problem

No contributor guide exists at any location GitHub surfaces (`.github/CONTRIBUTING.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md`). The repository has every enforced convention the contributing lens keys on: a build system, a test runner, a CI gate, and Conventional Commits with `!`/`BREAKING CHANGE:` footers. Contributors have to reverse-engineer all of it. Severity follows contributing.md step 7: absent guide plus enforced convention = High.

## Evidence

`git ls-files` has no CONTRIBUTING* at any of the three paths.
Build system: Makefile:11-14 `build:` with `-ldflags "-X main.version=$(VERSION) -X main.build=$(BUILD)"`.
Test runner: Makefile:16-17 `test:` → `go test ./...`; lint gate Makefile:19-21 (`go vet` + `golangci-lint`).
CI gate: .github/workflows/test-build.yml jobs `test-build-and-run` (vet, test, build) and `vulncheck` (fails on reachable vulns).
Commit convention: 56 of 57 commits use `type(scope)!: subject`, e.g. 95ca121 `fix(feed)!: …` with a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer.
Toolchain: go.mod `go 1.26.0` / `toolchain go1.27.3`, which CI reads via `go-version-file`.

## Impact

A contributor doesn't learn that `make lint` needs golangci-lint, that CI reads the Go version from go.mod, that `.editorconfig` is enforced, or that commits must follow Conventional Commits with `!` for config-contract breaks. Each surfaces only as a failed review or CI run.

## Fix

Scaffold `CONTRIBUTING.md` at the root, offered through the apply-fixes prompt, never written silently, with these sections from real tooling. Intro: from README line 3. Reporting issues: GitHub issues (no SECURITY.md exists). Development setup: Go toolchain per go.mod (`toolchain go1.27.3`); `git clone`, then `make build`. Code style: gofmt, `make lint` (go vet + golangci-lint, installed separately), `.editorconfig`. Testing: `make test` (`go test ./...`); scope with `go test -run TestName ./...`. Commit convention: Conventional Commits, `!` plus a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer when config keys, template format or output format change incompatibly. PR process: both CI jobs (`test-build-and-run`, `vulncheck`) must pass. License: MIT; contributions are under it.

## Resolution
Scaffolded root CONTRIBUTING.md from real tooling: setup (go.mod go/toolchain lines, make build), code style (gofmt, make lint, .editorconfig), testing (make test, offline suite), Conventional Commits with ! + BREAKING CHANGE for config/template/output breaks, PR gates (both CI jobs), MIT license. Re-reviewed against the final workflow; editorconfig-checker and markdownlint clean.
title: No CONTRIBUTING.md although the repo enforces a build, test runner, CI gate and commit convention

body:
## Problem Finding class: sast (manual, injection). `generateMarkdown` declares remote titles are "escaped at this boundary" so a feed cannot "forge week headings and links into the output document" (main.go:255-258), but `mdText` only escapes `\`, `[` and `]`. CommonMark raw HTML and autolinks both start with `<`, bind more tightly than link brackets, and pass through untouched. The no-link branch (main.go:279-286), documented as "leaving the entry as plain text" when a `javascript:`/`data:` link is rejected, re-acquires a live link from the title. ## Evidence main.go:62 `var mdTextEscaper = strings.NewReplacer(`\`, `\\`, "[", `\[`, "]", `\]`)` main.go:301-303 `func mdText(s string) string { return mdTextEscaper.Replace(strings.Join(strings.Fields(s), " ")) }` Reproduced offline with gofeed v1.5.0 + goldmark v1.8.6 (CommonMark), using mdText copied verbatim: - RSS item `<https://evil.example/phish>javascript:alert(1)` → gofeed Title ``; mdURL rejects the link, line 286 emits `- … @ : ` → goldmark **safe mode** renders ``. - Title `]]>` → rendered verbatim as `` inside the `` by any renderer allowing raw HTML (goldmark WithUnsafe, pandoc default, kramdown). - Title `

URGENT: verify your account

` → a forged heading in the HTML output, the exact case the comment claims is defused. Existing tests (main_test.go:138-152, 345-380) cover only brackets/backslashes/newlines. ## Impact A hostile or compromised feed can place clickable phishing links, tracking images, script-bearing tags and forged headings into the digest the README suggests mailing out (README "ProTip"). The autolink vector works even under goldmark's safe defaults, and it defeats the code's own rule that rejected-scheme items render as plain text. ## Fix Add `"<", `\<`` to the replacer at main.go:62 (CommonMark treats backslash-escaped ASCII punctuation as literal, which disables both raw HTML and autolinks): `strings.NewReplacer(`\`, `\\`, "[", `\[`, "]", `\]`, "<", `\<`)`. Verified with goldmark: all four payloads then render as `<…>` text. Extend the comment at main.go:50-61 to name the `<` constructs, and add TestMdText cases `{"html escaped", "", `\`}` and `{"autolink escaped", "", `\`}`. ## Resolution mdTextEscaper now also escapes "<" (main.go), disabling CommonMark raw HTML and autolinks; comment documents why. Tests: TestMdText "raw html escaped"/"autolink escaped" and TestGenerateMarkdownTitleCannotRelink (plain-text branch). Watched RED before the fix; mutation dropping the "<" pair fails both tests.
title: mdText leaves < unescaped, so feed titles inject raw HTML and autolinks into the digest

body:
## Problem

Fail-open masking fallback. Per-feed errors are logged and skipped (main.go:115-119), which is reasonable for a partial failure. But nothing distinguishes total failure: with zero feeds fetched, main still renders header+footer, overwrites `config.Output`, logs "Paperboy finished" and exits 0.

## Evidence

main.go:115-119
`articles, err := fetchArticles(fp, feedURL)`
`if err != nil { log.Printf("Error fetching articles from %s: %v", feedURL, err); continue }`
main.go:140-149 then unconditionally runs `generateMarkdown(...)`, `os.WriteFile(config.Output, ...)` and `log.Printf("Paperboy finished")`, and main returns (exit 0).
TestGenerateMarkdownNoArticles (main_test.go:401-407) shows the result is `"HEAD\n\nFOOT\n"`.
.github/workflows/test-build.yml:39-42 already notes "this step can pass while every feed is unreachable".

## Impact

A network outage, DNS failure or proxy misconfiguration on the cron host replaces the last good digest with an empty one and reports success. The README's cron recipe ("send the output to your email") then mails an empty newsletter, and nothing in the exit status lets a wrapper notice.

## Fix

Count successful fetches in the loop (`fetched++` after the error check). After the loop, `if fetched == 0 { log.Fatalf("all %d feeds failed; leaving %s untouched", len(config.Feeds), config.Output) }`, before generateMarkdown and WriteFile. Keep partial failures non-fatal as designed. Document the exit status in the README's cron section.

## Resolution
main's body extracted to run(configFile) error; run counts successful fetches and returns "fetching feeds: all N failed; <output> left untouched" before rendering or writing, so main exits non-zero and the previous digest survives. README cron section documents the exit status. TestRunAllFeedsFailedKeepsOutput watched RED; mutation removing the guard fails it.
title: Run exits 0 and overwrites the output with an empty digest when every feed fails

body:
## Problem

Finding class: dependency-vulnerability (standard library). go.mod pins `toolchain go1.27.3`. The Go vulnerability database now lists GO-2026-6859 ("HTTP/1 server crash due to MaxBytesReader header race in net/http"), found in net/http@go1.27.3 and fixed in go1.27.4. govulncheck reports it at symbol level through the feed-fetching path.

## Evidence

go.mod:5 `toolchain go1.27.3`.
govulncheck 1.9.0 (2026-11-11), exit 3: `Vulnerability #1: GO-2026-6859 … Found in: net/http@go1.27.3 Fixed in: net/http@go1.27.4`, trace `main.go:282:26: paperboy.fetchArticles calls gofeed.Parser.ParseURL, which eventually calls http.Client.Do`.
The same scan run earlier in this audit returned "No vulnerabilities found", so the advisory was published since.
`go list -m -versions golang.org/toolchain` includes `v0.0.1-go1.27.4.linux-amd64`.
.github/workflows/test-build.yml:77-86 fails the job on any error-level (reachable) govulncheck result.

## Impact

The vulncheck job fails on every push and PR until the toolchain moves. The advisory describes a server-side crash and paperboy runs only an HTTP client, so exploitability in normal use is low. The cost is a red, blocking CI gate plus a binary built from a toolchain with a known net/http defect.

## Fix

Change go.mod:5 to `toolchain go1.27.4` (GOTOOLCHAIN=auto and setup-go's `go-version-file` both pick it up), then re-run `govulncheck ./...` and confirm "No vulnerabilities found". Renovate's toolchain-directive rule would propose the same bump.

## Resolution
go.mod toolchain go1.27.3 -> go1.27.4 (user-approved after discovery mid-fix). go version reports go1.27.4; govulncheck ./... now "No vulnerabilities found" (exit 0).
title: Toolchain go1.27.3 ships net/http GO-2026-6859, which govulncheck reports reachable; CI vulncheck gate now fails

body:
## Problem

The doc comment and error message say the template is split on "the two "---" lines", but `strings.SplitN(string(data), "---", 3)` matches the substring anywhere: mid-line ("Intro --- read on"), or inside a longer thematic break ("----", "-----"). The text between the first two matches is discarded with no error, and the real separator lines move into the footer.

## Evidence

main.go:196 `parts := strings.SplitN(string(data), "---", 3)`
main.go:199 error text: `"template %s: want a header and footer separated by two --- lines, ..."`
Run with that exact SplitN/TrimSpace logic:
- `"# Weekly

Intro --- read on

---

---

Footer
"` → header `"# Weekly

Intro"`, footer `"---

Footer"`; " read on" lost, a stray rule added before the footer.
- `"# Weekly

----

Intro paragraph

---

---

Footer
"` → header `"# Weekly"`; "Intro paragraph" lost.
Both return 3 sections, so no error fires. main_test.go:265-294 tests only templates with no other dashes.

## Impact

An ordinary Markdown header (a `----` horizontal rule, an em-dash typed as `---`) silently loses content from every generated newsletter. Nothing reports it, and the output still looks plausible.

## Fix

Split on separator lines only: `var templateSep = regexp.MustCompile(`(?m)^---[ 	]*?$`)` at package scope, then `parts := templateSep.Split(string(data), 3)`. Keep the `len(parts) != 3` check. Add TestLoadTemplateValid cases for a mid-line `---` and a `----` rule in the header, asserting the header text survives.

## Resolution
loadTemplate splits on templateSep `(?m)^---[ 	]*?$` (separator lines only) instead of the bare substring. TestLoadTemplateSplitsOnSeparatorLinesOnly (mid-line dashes, "----" rule, CRLF) watched RED for the two substring cases; mutation restoring SplitN fails it.
title: loadTemplate splits on any "---" substring, silently discarding header text

body:
## Problem

`domainRe` accepts only `[a-z0-9-]`. url.Parse keeps IDN hosts in Unicode, so the regexp's leftmost match starts after the last non-ASCII rune and returns a different, plausible-looking domain. The same happens for `_` labels. This is the same class as the "xample.com" bug the comment at main.go:326-330 says was fixed.

## Evidence

main.go:48 `var domainRe = regexp.MustCompile(`([a-z0-9\-]+\.)+[a-z0-9\-]+`)`
Run with getURLDomain copied verbatim (main.go:331-343):
- `https://bücher.example/post` → `cher.example`
- `https://www.müller.example/a` → `ller.example`
- `https://my_blog.example.com/a` → `blog.example.com`
- `https://xn--bcher-kva.example/post` → `xn--bcher-kva.example` (punycode works, Unicode does not)
TestGetURLDomain (main_test.go:112-136) has no non-ASCII case.

## Impact

The digest attributes articles from IDN sites (common for German, Nordic and CJK publishers) to a different domain, which misleads readers about the source of a link.

## Fix

Widen the character class to Unicode letters and digits: `regexp.MustCompile(`([\p{L}\p{N}_-]+\.)+[\p{L}\p{N}_-]+`)` (input is already lower-cased at main.go:332). Add test cases `{"IDN host", "https://bücher.example/p", "bücher.example"}` and `{"underscore label", "https://my_blog.example.com/a", "my_blog.example.com"}`.

## Resolution
domainRe label class widened to [\p{L}\p{N}_-]. TestGetURLDomain cases "IDN host" (bücher.example), "IDN host with www" (müller.example), "underscore label" watched RED; existing "no domain present" still returns "". Mutation restoring the ASCII class fails the test.
title: getURLDomain truncates hosts with non-ASCII or underscore labels to a wrong domain

body:
## Problem RSS 2.0 makes every item element optional ("at least one of title or description must be present"), and gofeed returns `Title == ""` and `Link == ""` for such items. generateMarkdown interpolates both unconditionally: an empty title produces `[](url)`, which renders as an anchor with no text, and an empty link produces an empty URLDomain, so the line reads `@ :`. ## Evidence main.go:282 `fmt.Fprintf(&output, "- %s @ %s: [%s](%s)\n", date, article.URLDomain, title, link)` main.go:286 `fmt.Fprintf(&output, "- %s @ %s: %s\n", date, article.URLDomain, title)` gofeed v1.5.0 parse of `Untitled microblog posthttps://e.example/c…` → `title=""`; of `No link item…` → `link=""`. goldmark render of the resulting lines: `
  • 2006-01-02 @ e.example:
    • ` (no visible text) and `
  • 2006-01-02 @ : No link item
    • `. ## Impact Title-less feeds (microblog and Mastodon-style RSS) contribute dated bullets with nothing to read or click, so their articles are effectively missing from the digest. Link-less items get a malformed attribution. ## Fix In itemsToArticles, when `strings.TrimSpace(item.Title) == ""`, fall back to the domain (or "(untitled)"), so the label is never empty. In generateMarkdown, emit the `@ ` segment only when `article.URLDomain != ""`. Add a generateMarkdown test with an empty Title and an empty URL asserting neither `[](` nor `@ :` appears. ## Resolution generateMarkdown renders "(untitled)" when the escaped title is empty and omits the " @ domain" segment when URLDomain is empty. TestGenerateMarkdownOptionalFields (untitled, whitespace-only title, no link) watched RED; mutations of either branch fail it.
title: Untitled items render as an invisible empty link; link-less items render "@ :"

body:
## Problem

Crash-window data loss. `os.WriteFile` opens the existing output with O_TRUNC and then writes. Any failure after the truncate (ENOSPC, EDQUOT, the process being killed mid-write) leaves a truncated or partial file in place of the previous digest.

## Evidence

main.go:144 `if err := os.WriteFile(config.Output, []byte(output), 0644); err != nil {`
os.WriteFile is documented as "If the file does not exist, WriteFile creates it with permissions perm (before umask); otherwise WriteFile truncates it before writing".

## Impact

The previous run's digest can't be rebuilt once feeds have rolled their items off. A cron chain using `;` instead of `&&` would ship the partial file.

## Fix

Write to a sibling temp file and rename over the target: `tmp, err := os.CreateTemp(filepath.Dir(config.Output), ".paperboy-*")`; write; `tmp.Close()`; `os.Chmod(tmp.Name(), 0o644)`; `os.Rename(tmp.Name(), config.Output)`; on any error `os.Remove(tmp.Name())` and log.Fatalf. Rename within one directory is atomic on POSIX filesystems.

## Resolution
New writeFileAtomic: CreateTemp beside the (symlink-resolved) target, write, close, chmod 0644, rename; temp removed on any failure. run uses it. Tests: ReplacesWholeFile (old reader keeps old bytes, mode 0644, no temp left), CleansUpOnFailure, FollowsSymlink (self-review caught that a bare rename replaced a symlinked output; fixed test-first). Mutations (in-place write, wrong mode, no cleanup, no symlink resolve) each caught.
title: Output is written in place, so a failed write destroys the previous digest

body:
## Problem

The case is labelled as the regression test for unknown-key rejection, but its fixture misspells `output` as `outout`. With KnownFields disabled the misspelled key is ignored, `Output` stays empty, and the required-field check fails instead, so the test asserts only `err != nil` and cannot tell which check fired.

## Evidence

main_test.go:311-313
`// Regression: a misspelled key previously unmarshalled cleanly and`
`// failed only after every feed had been fetched.`
`"unknown key": "feeds:\n  - https://e.com/f\ntemplate: template.md\noutout: output.md\n",`
main_test.go:322 `if _, err := loadConfig(...); err == nil {`
Mutation run: deleted main.go:168 `dec.KnownFields(true)` in a scratch copy → `--- PASS: TestLoadConfigRejectsBadInput/unknown_key`.

## Impact

Removing or breaking `KnownFields(true)` would ship green. Misspelled optional keys would then be silently ignored, and the README's promise that "an unrecognised key is an error" would stop holding with no test failing.

## Fix

Use a fixture that is otherwise valid and adds an extra key: `"feeds:\n  - https://e.com/f\ntemplate: template.md\noutput: output.md\nextra: x\n"`. Also assert the error names it: `strings.Contains(err.Error(), "extra")` (yaml.v3 reports `field extra not found in type main.Config`). Re-run the KnownFields mutation and confirm the case fails.

## Resolution
Replaced the "unknown key" table case with TestLoadConfigRejectsUnknownKey: otherwise-complete fixture plus `extra: x`, asserting the error names "extra". Mutation deleting dec.KnownFields(true) now fails it (it passed before).
title: "unknown key" regression test still passes with KnownFields removed

body:
## Problem

Coverage hole on a critical path. ISO-week grouping, the core of the output's structure, is inline in main() and cannot be tested. fetchArticles, which applies MaxByteSize and the User-Agent, is never exercised, even though net/http/httptest would allow it offline.

## Evidence

`go test -coverprofile` → `main.go:86: main 0.0%`, `main.go:208: fetchArticles 0.0%`, total 60.2%.
main.go:125-129 `year, week := article.PublishAt.UTC().ISOWeek()` … `id := fmt.Sprintf("%d-%02d", year, week)`. No test references ISOWeek, the year boundary or maxFeedBytes.

## Impact

A regression such as `Year()` instead of the ISO year (2024-12-30 belongs to 2025-01), or dropping `fp.MaxByteSize`, would pass CI. The live smoke step can't catch either, because it exits 0 regardless.

## Fix

Extract `func groupByWeek(articles []Article, into map[string][]Article)` from main.go:124-130 and test it with 2024-12-30T00:00:00Z → "2025-01" and 2027-01-01T00:00:00Z → "2026-53". Add a fetchArticles test using `httptest.NewServer`: one handler returns a small RSS body and asserts `r.Header.Get("User-Agent")` starts with "paperboy/"; another streams more than `fp.MaxByteSize` (set it low in the test) and asserts `errors.Is(err, gofeed.ErrResponseTooLarge)`.

## Resolution
Covered through run() with httptest servers instead of extracting groupByWeek (simpler, same protection): TestRunGroupsByISOWeek (2024-12-30 -> 2025-01, 2027-01-01 -> 2026-53, verified with date +%G-%V; one feed failing), TestRunSendsUserAgent, TestRunCapsFeedSize (feed 1 byte over maxFeedBytes). Mutations Year()-instead-of-ISO-year, dropped UserAgent, dropped MaxByteSize each caught. Coverage 60.2% -> 88.6%; fetchArticles 100%, run 91.7%.
title: Week grouping and the HTTP fetch path have no tests (main and fetchArticles at 0% coverage)

body:
## Problem

The config parser depends on `gopkg.in/yaml.v3`, whose upstream repository (go-yaml/yaml) was archived on 2025-04-01 with a README headed "THIS PROJECT IS UNMAINTAINED". Maintenance continues under the YAML organization as `go.yaml.in/yaml/v3`, which has the same API.

## Evidence

go.mod:9 `gopkg.in/yaml.v3 v3.0.1`; main.go:27 `"gopkg.in/yaml.v3"`.
`gh api repos/go-yaml/yaml` → `archived=true pushed=2025-04-01T17:00:11Z`; README@v3: "# THIS PROJECT IS UNMAINTAINED".
`gh api repos/yaml/go-yaml` → `archived=false`, "The YAML org maintained fork of https://github.com/go-yaml/yaml", tags v3.0.4–v3.0.6.
govulncheck 1.9.0: "No vulnerabilities found" today. The risk is future fixes not landing, not a current CVE.

## Impact

Any future parser bug or CVE in yaml.v3 (it parses operator-supplied config) will not be fixed upstream, and Renovate can't offer a release that will never exist.

## Fix

`go get go.yaml.in/yaml/v3@v3.0.4` (or the latest v3 tag), change main.go:27 to `"go.yaml.in/yaml/v3"`, then `go mod tidy`. `NewDecoder` and `KnownFields` are unchanged, so no other code edits are needed. Run `go test ./...`.

## Resolution
Migrated to go.yaml.in/yaml/v3 v3.0.6 (YAML org maintained fork); import changed in main.go, go mod tidy leaves no gopkg.in/yaml in go.mod/go.sum. go mod verify ok; full suite incl. TestLoadConfigRejectsUnknownKey passes.
title: Direct dependency gopkg.in/yaml.v3 is archived and declared unmaintained

body:
## Problem

The MIT license lives at `.github/LICENSE.md`. GitHub's license detection only reads a license file at the repository root, so the public repository presents as having no license, even though every source file carries `SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT`.

## Evidence

`gh api repos/ivuorinen/paperboy` → `private=false license=null`.
`gh api repos/ivuorinen/paperboy/license` → HTTP 404 Not Found.
`gh api repos/ivuorinen/paperboy/community/profile` → `files.license` absent.
`git ls-files` has no root LICENSE*; the only license file is .github/LICENSE.md.

## Impact

Visitors, dependency scanners and license-compliance tooling read the project as "no license" (all rights reserved), which discourages reuse the MIT grant intends to permit. Tools that key off root license files (GitHub's sidebar and API, SBOM generators) record it as unlicensed.

## Fix

`git mv .github/LICENSE.md LICENSE.md` and update the README link at .github/README.md:62 from `(LICENSE.md)` to `(../LICENSE.md)`. Then confirm `gh api repos/ivuorinen/paperboy/license --jq .license.spdx_id` prints `MIT`.

## Resolution
git mv .github/LICENSE.md LICENSE.md (rename staged, not committed); README link updated to ../LICENSE.md; CONTRIBUTING links LICENSE.md. GitHub's license API can only confirm detection after this is pushed.
title: License file under .github/ is not detected: GitHub reports the public repo as unlicensed

body:
## Problem

`.editorconfig` applies `max_line_length = 160` to every file (`[*]`), but tracked files exceed it: one hand-written Makefile line, and every line of the generated findings ledger and index. The store's generator cannot wrap a JSONL record or a table row, so the store will violate the rule on every audit run unless the directory is given its own section.

## Evidence

editorconfig-checker 4.0.2 over `git ls-files`: 24 errors.
- Makefile:9 — 166 columns (the `help` recipe's grep/printf one-liner).
- docs/audit/findings/resolved.jsonl:1-18 — 1607 to 3280 columns (one JSON record per line by design).
- docs/audit/findings/INDEX.md:15-19 — 165 to 231 columns (table rows).
The five finding files created by this run add 21 more violations.
.editorconfig:3,9 `[*]` … `max_line_length = 160`.

## Impact

An editorconfig check in CI or a pre-commit hook fails on files no one can hand-wrap, and the real hand-written violation in the Makefile is buried among generated noise.

## Fix

1) Add to .editorconfig: `[docs/audit/findings/**]` then `max_line_length = off`. EditorConfig's spec value `off` is the standard way to exempt generated content, and editorconfig-checker honours it. 2) Wrap Makefile:9 with a backslash continuation (e.g. break before `| sort`), keeping it tab-indented per `[Makefile]`.

## Resolution
.editorconfig gains [docs/audit/findings/**] max_line_length = off (user-approved config change); Makefile:9 wrapped with a backslash continuation, `make help` output byte-identical before/after. editorconfig-checker over all tracked and new files: 0 errors.
title: Committed files violate .editorconfig max_line_length = 160 (Makefile:9 and the generated findings store)

body:
## Problem

Finding class: misconfiguration. Both jobs set job-level `permissions`, but the workflow sets none at top level. The comment at lines 13-15 justifies this with "a new job cannot silently inherit a scope nobody chose for it", which is the opposite of GitHub's behaviour: a job without its own `permissions` key inherits the workflow-level block, and with none, the repository's default GITHUB_TOKEN scope (which can be read-write).

## Evidence

checkov 3.4.3 CKV2_GHA_1 ("Ensure top-level permissions are not set to write-all", graph check ReadOnlyTopLevelPermissions) FAILED on /.github/workflows/test-build.yml lines 16-17.
test-build.yml:13-15:
`# Declared per job rather than once at workflow level: a job-level block is`
`# explicit about what that job may do, and a new job cannot silently`
`# inherit a scope nobody chose for it.`
No `permissions:` key exists between `on:` (line 4) and `jobs:` (line 10).

## Impact

Adding a third job without copying a permissions block grants it the repository default token, possibly write, on every push and PR. The comment steers maintainers away from the one setting that would prevent that.

## Fix

Add `permissions: {}` at workflow top level (between `on:` and `jobs:`), keep both job-level blocks, and rewrite the comment: "Top level grants nothing, so a job without its own block gets no token scope; each job opts into exactly what it needs."

## Resolution
Workflow now sets top-level `permissions: {}`; job-level blocks kept; wrong comment replaced with an accurate one. checkov github_actions: 0 failed (CKV2_GHA_1 passes); zizmor excessive-permissions gone; actionlint clean.
title: Workflow has no top-level permissions block; comment wrongly claims new jobs cannot inherit a default scope

body:
## Problem

The checkout step does not set `persist-credentials: false`, so the job token is written to `.git/config`, where every subsequent step can read it. That includes `make build` and `./paperboy`, which processes untrusted third-party feed content. No later step needs git credentials.

## Evidence

test-build.yml:19 `- uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1` with no `with:` block.
zizmor 1.31.1 (offline): `warning[artipacked]: credential persistence through GitHub Actions artifacts --> .github/workflows/test-build.yml:19:9 … does not set persist-credentials: false`.

## Impact

A compromised build-time dependency, or a future step that uploads the workspace as an artifact, can exfiltrate the token. Today's scope is `contents: read`, so the blast radius grows with any future permission change.

## Fix

Add to the checkout step: `with:` / `persist-credentials: false`. Nothing later in the job runs git commands that need it.

## Resolution
actions/checkout step sets persist-credentials: false with a comment explaining no later step runs git. zizmor (pedantic, offline) no longer reports artipacked.
title: actions/checkout persists the GITHUB_TOKEN into .git/config for every later step

body:
## Problem

Non-gating check. `make lint` defines the project's lint gate as `go vet` plus `golangci-lint run`, but CI runs only `go vet`. Nothing anywhere checks gofmt: golangci-lint v2 `run` with no config runs no formatters. Code that fails the repo's own lint target, or isn't gofmt-clean, merges with CI green.

## Evidence

Makefile:19-21 `lint: # Run go vet and golangci-lint.` / `go vet ./...` / `golangci-lint run ./...`
test-build.yml:27-31 `- name: Vet` `run: go vet ./...` and `- name: Test` `run: go test ./...`; no golangci-lint or gofmt step anywhere in the workflow.
No .golangci.yml in `git ls-files`.

## Impact

errcheck, ineffassign, staticcheck and unused regressions, plus formatting drift, reach main undetected. Each contributor's local `make lint` then fails on code CI accepted.

## Fix

Add steps after Vet: `- name: gofmt` / `run: test -z "$(gofmt -l .)" || { gofmt -l .; exit 1; }`, and `- uses: golangci/golangci-lint-action@<sha> # vX` pinned by SHA like the other actions (Renovate will track it). Alternatively run `make lint` after installing golangci-lint, so CI and the Makefile cannot drift.

## Resolution
Added "Check formatting" (fails on any gofmt -l output) and "Lint" (golangci/golangci-lint-action@ba0d7d2e… # v9.3.0, SHA verified against the tag) steps. Linter version pinned via GOLANGCI_LINT_VERSION v2.15.0 with the shared preset's customManagers:githubActionsVersions renovate comment (regex verified to extract it). actionlint clean.
title: CI never runs the repo's lint gate (golangci-lint) or a gofmt check

body:
## Problem

Checked against Conventional Commits (no CLAUDE.md, CONTRIBUTING or release-please config defines another standard), all 57 commits in the full history (no tags) were examined message-versus-diff. Defects: spurious-breaking on five CI-action bumps whose only hunk is a workflow `uses:` SHA; type-overstatement (`feat`) on three toolchain/CI bumps that add no user-facing behaviour; scope-lie on two x/net updates whose hunks also raise the `go` language floor, one of them silently undoing the floor 8dc09ea set deliberately. The same change class is labelled inconsistently: action majors #6/#7 had no `!`; dependency updates alternate `fix(deps)` and `chore(deps)`.

## Evidence

spurious-breaking (only hunk: .github/workflows/test-build.yml `uses:` line): d1e4a84 `feat(github-action)!: Update actions/checkout (v4 → v5)`, 14cd51f `chore(deps)!: update actions/setup-go (v5 → v6)`, a65fa57 `chore(deps)!: update actions/checkout (v5 → v6)`, b856395 `chore(deps)!: update actions/checkout action (v6.0.3 → v7.0.0)`, 3360f6f `chore(deps)!: update actions/setup-go action (v6.5.0 → v7.0.0)`. Contrast ca49494/d10f087 (same kind of major bump, no `!`).
type-overstatement: 15e7c84 `feat(github-action): update go (1.22.12 → 1.24.1)` (only `go-version: "1.22"`→`"1.24"` in the workflow); 1b45ddf `feat(deps): update go to v1.25.0` (workflow go-version + `toolchain` line only); d1e4a84 as above.
scope-lie: 569d15e `chore(deps): update module golang.org/x/net to v0.36.0 [security]` also `-go 1.22.2 +go 1.23.0`; 0e49c66 `…x/net (v0.58.0 → v0.60.0) [security]` also `-go 1.25.0 +go 1.26.0`.
Version consequence: as-labeled range = major; corrected = major (95ca121 `fix(feed)!` legitimately breaks the config contract: `yaml.Unmarshal` → `KnownFields(true)` + required fields). No release tooling exists (no tags, no release-please/goreleaser/CHANGELOG), so no release is mis-versioned today. Severity is Low rather than the guide's Medium because the changelog consumer that premise assumes is absent. All commits are pushed (origin/main).
Hygiene only (Advisory, no consequence): e013b25 `Initial commit` (no type), 3e51f6f `chore: tweaks` (non-descriptive).

## Impact

History misreports CI maintenance as breaking changes and features, so `git log --grep '!:'` or any future release-please adoption would compute a major for a CI bump and list toolchain bumps as features. The floor change in 0e49c66 reversed a documented decision without a word in its title.

## Fix

History is pushed: do not rewrite it. Fix forward in the Renovate configuration (the shared `github>ivuorinen/renovate-config` preset, or a local `packageRules` override in .github/renovate.json): set `{"matchManagers": ["github-actions"], "semanticCommitType": "ci", "semanticCommitScope": "actions"}` and do not apply a breaking `!` prefix to github-actions or toolchain updates. Set `{"matchDepNames": ["go"], "semanticCommitType": "chore"}`. If release-please is ever adopted, add a `Release-As:` correction commit pinning the first version.

## Resolution
No repo change made: the shared preset ivuorinen/renovate-config already carries the forward fix (rule "Label majors, nothing more. No update is marked breaking", enforced by its test/check-commit-messages.mjs; github-actions scoped "actions"), confirmed by commits #49-#57 using chore(actions). This should have been checked before filing. Pushed history is not rewritten per the commits lens; no release tooling consumes it.
title: Renovate commits carry spurious breaking markers and feat types on CI-only and toolchain bumps
